Zupanja Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Županja, Croatia

Not demolished. Županja's Jewish population reached 88 by 1931, about 5 percent of the town before WWII; none remained afterward. The town's most notable Jewish native was Amiel Shomrony (born Emil Schwarz, 1917–2009), a Holocaust survivor who later served as cantor for the Jewish community in Zagreb and as secretary to Zagreb's Chief Rabbi, Miroslav Šalom Freiberger, during WWII; Shomrony became widely revered in modern Croatia for his public defense of Archbishop Aloysius Stepinac, who himself saved several Jewish families during the Holocaust despite facing repeated accusations of wartime nationalist sympathies. This cemetery, established at the end of the 19th century, was confiscated and closed after WWII, though a few tombstones and a mausoleum survive, ranging from 1879 to 1935.
